transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-18
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Marta Reyes (Novus Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Novus Platform), Priya Patel (Novus Security), Carlos Mendes (Novus Data)
Shared links: https://redwood.app/pinned-models (shared), /s/novus/poc-results.xlsx (internal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Reviewed latest head-to-heads for redwood-gpt variants and quantized candidates; discussed pinning v1.3.2 for production canary and fallback to v1.2.8 for heavy tails.
- Customer concerned about 99th percentile latency and encryption/KMS path on private deployment.
- Action items include Redwood sharing spreadsheet + quant notes, Novus running dedicated staging benchmarks, and security follow-up.

[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll be quick with the agenda — recap of last week's results, model selection for canary/pin, rollback/fallback options, and next steps. Marta, Liam, you still good with the 45?
[00:12] Marta Reyes: Yeah that's good. We mostly want to focus on 99th pct, cost delta, and the pinning strategy.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Also the network side — the VPC tests we kicked off last night, we should sync if there were any surprises.
[00:24] Jordan Park: Great. Samira, did you want to kick off with the updated perf sheet?
[00:28] Samira Khan: Sure. I pulled the numbers into the shared sheet, link in the chat. Quick note — the test harness we used is the same as last time but we increased sample size for tail latency. The headline: redwood-gpt-medium-v1.3.2 (float32) giving mean latency ~120ms on our dedicated 4xA100 profile, 95th ~190ms, 99th ~320ms for 512-token prompts. The quantized v1.3.2-q8 gives mean 85ms, 95th 140ms, 99th 260ms but with a small drop in long-form coherency on the edge cases in eval set.
[01:10] Carlos Mendes: small drop meaning like hallucination rates or token-level perplexity?
[01:15] Samira Khan: It's more on structured extraction tasks — we saw a ~3% drop in field-extraction F1 on our eval prompts, so it's noticeable but not catastrophic.
[01:22] Marta Reyes: Hmm. For Novus, those fields are kinda important, but if the delta is small maybe acceptable if latency/cost tradeoff is big. What's the cost delta?
[01:31] Samira Khan: On our cost model, quantized path is about 35-40% cheaper per token for the dedicated pool due to memory and batch improvements. For hosted, it's similar once caching and batching are in play.
[01:40] Ethan Li: One add — we saw some variability with KV cache warm/cold behavior in the test harness; for certain sequences the 99th jumps when cache misses align. We're flagging that in the sheet as 'KV cache noise' (sometimes transcribed as KV cash in the logs, apologies).
[01:54] Liam O'Connor: Are those cache misses something we can control from the app side? We rely on short-lived sessions a lot.
[02:02] Samira Khan: It depends. If sessions are very short you lose prefix reuse benefits; we can recommend conservative batching and pre-warming heuristics. For dedicated you can bump the warm capacity but that increases cost.
[02:14] Marta Reyes: Ok. On pinning — you recommended pin v1.3.2 for the canary and keep v1.2.8 as fallback? Samira, can you walk us through the rollback/compatibility matrix?
[02:24] Samira Khan: Yeah. v1.3.2 introduces a minor tokenizer change and a few attention-fusion optimizations; it's backwards-compatible for most prompts, but there are corner cases. We created model aliases in the catalog: redwood-gpt-medium-v1.3.2 and redwood-gpt-medium-v1.2.8. Our routing can do policy-based fallback — e.g., route to v1.3.2 normally, but if latency exceeds SLO or token cost per request spikes, auto-fallback to v1.2.8 or to a cheaper quantized variant.
[02:50] Priya Patel: Just to clarify — will fallback preserve the same API schema? We can't have different response formats for downstream processors.
[02:58] Samira Khan: Good question. Both the v1.3.2 and v1.2.8 variants use the same output schema. We recommend a small compatibility test suite to run across versions to confirm.
[03:10] Marta Reyes: What's the expected quality delta between v1.3.2 float32 and v1.2.8?
[03:15] Samira Khan: v1.3.2 is slightly better on abstractive summarization and instruction-following; v1.2.8 is pretty stable on extraction. We saw in your eval set: v1.3.2 +1.5% exact match on the answer set, but v1.2.8 had marginally better stability on structured fields.
[03:33] Carlos Mendes: Could we instead pin v1.3.2 for the UX paths and keep v1.2.8 pinned for the ETL/extraction endpoints? Split routing by route?
[03:41] Jordan Park: Totally doable — per-route pinning is supported. That might actually be the safest approach for Novus.
[03:47] Liam O'Connor: Our main worry is cost across high-TPS endpoints. If we put v1.3.2 on user-facing chat where latency matters and v1.2.8 on batch extraction, that sounds right. But can we also program an automatic rollback if 99th pct breach persists for X minutes?
[04:00] Samira Khan: Yes, you can set automatic fallback rules — e.g., if 99th > 300ms for 5 minutes, roll back to fallback variant. We usually recommend a canary window and alerting first, then auto-fallback as a last-resort.
[04:12] Marta Reyes: What's the smallest canary cohort we can do? We have compliance constraints around data routing — some PII must stay in region.
[04:20] Ethan Li: You can do a 1-5% traffic canary. For PII constraints, we can ensure routing by region and VPC; our private control plane supports per-tenant routing rules.
[04:30] Priya Patel: Speaking of compliance — quick note, we're evaluating KMS integration. The docs you sent included the HSM/KMS flow, but we need to confirm the envelope encryption for logs and stored KV.
[04:41] Jordan Park: Right, Jordan here — we will follow up with the security doc pack. Samira, can you summarize the KMS path we use for private?
[04:48] Samira Khan: For Private we support customer-managed KMS — you can bring your key in AWS KMS or an external HSM (we have a documented flow). Logs can be encrypted at rest and transit; audit logs are sent to your S3 or SIEM endpoint. We'll attach the exact diagram.
[04:59] Priya Patel: And SOC 2/ISO? We saw high-levels but we might need the SOC2 type II report redacted for legal review.
[05:07] Jordan Park: Noted — I'll put that as an item, expect within 2 business days.
[05:12] Marta Reyes: Back to model selection: can you do a quick walkthrough of the downgrade path — quantize first or fallback to older float model? Which gives fewer regressions?
[05:21] Samira Khan: In our experience, going from float32 to q8 gives biggest win but highest small-regression risk; fallback to older float is safer quality-wise but less cost savings. So the common pattern: primary = v1.3.2 float32, fallback1 = v1.3.2-q8 (if cost spike), fallback2 = v1.2.8 float (if quality/regression). You can chain them.
[05:38] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. Can you show the exact routing policy we tested?
[05:43] Ethan Li: I posted the sample canary policy in the doc — it looks like: 5% traffic -> v1.3.2, monitor 5m windows, if 99th > threshold then switch 100% to fallback route. It's parameterized.
[05:56] Marta Reyes: About the pinned versions — is pinning a permanent lock or reversible? We want to be able to rollback quickly during incidents.
[06:04] Samira Khan: Pinning just sets the catalog alias to that exact model; you can change it programmatically or via the console and rollbacks are immediate. We also keep previous versions in the catalog so you can re-point.
[06:13] Liam O'Connor: Ok good. We ran one of your benchmark scripts overnight on our side — quick note, we saw a strange spike around 03:00 where 99th jumped to 600ms, logs showed a transient network blip to the region. Might be unrelated to the model.
[06:27] Jordan Park: That's consistent with infra noise; good call to cross-check with network logs.
[06:31] Priya Patel: For the privacy path — if we route to Redwood Private in our VPC, does any unencrypted payload traverse Redwood-managed network?
[06:39] Samira Khan: No — in Private, data plane lives in your VPC, control plane talks over a management channel but we don't persist payloads. We'll send the architecture diagram and specifics.
[06:49] Marta Reyes: Great. Any objections from Novus to the recommended pin: v1.3.2 float for UX, v1.2.8 float for extraction, and v1.3.2-q8 available as cost fallback?
[06:59] Priya Patel: Sounds okay pending SOC2 docs and KMS confirmation.
[07:04] Carlos Mendes: I want to run a small A/B on the extraction route just to quantify the structured field diffs — can we pin v1.2.8 for that route for two weeks?
[07:12] Jordan Park: Absolutely. We'll schedule that and add monitoring hooks into the eval set.
[07:16] Marta Reyes: On instrumentation — we want to instrument token-level cost, 95/99 latency and metric for extraction F1; can we get per-route telemetry?
[07:24] Ethan Li: Yes, console exposes per-route metrics and you can push your own eval hooks to the metrics API. We'll add the eval suite we used to the shared folder.
[07:32] Liam O'Connor: Last thing — can we run the dedicated staging benchmark for 48h to capture diurnal effects? We'll run the script and share logs.
[07:40] Jordan Park: Good plan. We'll provide the benchmark harness and a short README.
[07:44] Samira Khan: For expectations — if you run 48h we should get stable 95/99 numbers; please include the raw p95/p99 and token distribution.
[07:52] Marta Reyes: Ok. Anything else we should capture?
[07:55] Priya Patel: Legal asked about data residency — confirm that Private keeps data in-customer region.
[07:59] Jordan Park: Confirmed; will include in the follow-up doc.
[08:03] Jordan Park: Alright, recap of action items — I'll shoot the pinned perf sheet + SOC2 pointer; Samira will add quant notes; Liam will run benchmarks; Priya will review KMS doc. We'll meet same time next week.
[08:17] Marta Reyes: Thanks everyone, that works.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: Medium — some proper nouns and acronyms (KV cache, A100) are sometimes mistranscribed; timestamps approximate.

Referenced assets: pinned-models spreadsheet (link above), security pack (will be shared), routing policy example (in doc).
